Now produce final response.<|end_think|>**Step 1 – Count all possible circular arrangements**  

There are six balls: two blue (B), two red (R) and two white (W).  
When balls of the same colour are indistinguishable, the number of distinct circular
arrangements is the number of circular permutations of a multiset:

\[
N_{\text{total}}=\frac{(6-1)!}{2!\,2!\,2!}
               =\frac{5!}{8}
               =\frac{120}{8}=15 .
\]

(If the six balls were labelled individually, the total would be \((6-1)!=120\); the
probability turns out the same, so we may work with the indistinguishable case.)

---

**Step 2 – Impose the adjacency condition**  

“All balls of the same colour are adjacent’’ means that each colour appears as a
pair of consecutive balls around the circle.  
Thus the six balls must form three blocks

\[
\underbrace{BB}_{\text{blue block}},\quad 
\underbrace{RR}_{\text{red block}},\quad 
\underbrace{WW}_{\text{white block}} .
\]

Treat each block as a single object.  We now have three distinct objects to arrange
circularly, so the number of admissible circular arrangements is

\[
N_{\text{fav}}=(3-1)! =2 .
\]

(If the balls were labelled, each block could be ordered in \(2!\) ways, giving
\(2\cdot 2!\cdot 2!\cdot 2!=2\cdot8=16\) favourable linear arrangements, which again
reduces to the same ratio.)

---

**Step 3 – Form the probability**  

\[
P=\frac{N_{\text{fav}}}{N_{\text{total}}}
  =\frac{2}{15}.
\]

Thus the chance that, when the six balls are placed at random around a circle,
the two balls of each colour sit next to each other is  

\[
\boxed{\dfrac{2}{15}}.
\]<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
